text:
mia: Quick follow-up from the impersonation RFC — a few edge cases popped up during the Dedicated rollout. want to align on rate-limiting attribution and audit trails.
alex: what scenarios are you seeing?
mia: two main things: 1) service A needs to call service B on behalf of user U (act-as). 2) service-to-service background jobs that should be limited by project quota, not user. both need clear audit and quota attribution.
sam: for act-as we suggested short-lived impersonation tokens via token-exchange (STS). that gives a clear 'actor' in the token and easy audit. downside: more token churn + cache complexity.
claire: question: do we want billing/quota to follow the original service principal or the impersonated user? product needs predictable quotas for tenant isolation.
alex: opt-in model? default follow service principal for quota, but include an attribute when act-as is used so billing can switch if tenant requests. avoids accidental quota bypass.
mia: I like default service-principal for background jobs. for interactive flows (user triggers) we can let act-as flip billing if downstream enforces tenant isolation. need policy UX in Console.
sam: rate limiter implementation detail: our current token-key -> rate-bucket mapping uses API key id. If we allow ephemeral tokens that don't map to an API key, we need to annotate exchange responses with parent_key_id. e.g., 
```
X-Parent-Key: key_abc123
```
so limiter and logs can attribute.
alex: +1. keep parent_key_id embedded in both token claims and response header. also add jti to correlate.
mia: audit trail: require immutable audit events for both original principal and impersonated actor. events should include fields: actor, impersonator, reason, request_id.
claire: product: expose an admin toggle per project to allow impersonation and a retention policy for audit logs. legal wants 365d by default for enterprise.
sam: encryption/keys: exchanges should be signed by KMS and accept only from trusted IPs when in Dedicated. we should fail open or closed? prefer fail-closed for security but that could impact resilience during KMS outages.
alex: tradeoff: fail-closed prevents privilege escalation but breaks availability. maybe fail-closed for high-sensitivity endpoints and fail-open with alarm for low-sensitivity. we can tag routes with sensitivity levels.
mia: rollout plan idea: 1) implement parent_key_id plumbing + audit events 2) enable impersonation in Dedicated as opt-in 3) run canary where act-as tokens are created but rejected unless flag set (dry-run) 4) monitor false positives.
claire: timeline OK. product will add console toggle + UI text for legal.
jinx-bot: deploybot: rotation-schedule created: impersonation-plumbing v1 -> canary -> 2% traffic on 2064123500.
sam: one more: rotation + revocation. ephemeral tokens revoke easy, but parent key revocation must cascade and invalidate existing impersonation tokens. need TTL and introspection endpoint.
alex: agree — add introspect endpoint and publish recommended TTL (e.g., 15m) for act-as tokens. longer TTL only with explicit approval.
mia: outstanding action items: @alex add parent_key_id header + claim, @sam add rate-limiter mapping for parent, @claire add console toggle + retention options, I'll draft follow-up RFC with rollout steps.
claire: noted, will sync with legal on retention.
alex: will open PR for token-exchange header and claim.
sam: will prototype limiter changes, pinging @eng-sre for load tests.
mia: thanks all. :thumbsup:
